commits: 758170f fix: router follow-ups from the review of the fourth panel's fixes
2e4090d fix: a control whose target only a redirect answers is not a dead link

items.problem: router (f): guards that a named-outlet route runs while it stays open were missed. canMatch runs again on every navigation, and with runGuardsAndResolvers 'always' so do canActivate and the resolvers. An absolute link keeps the root's other outlets, so the edge was must when it should not be (extract.ts closing).
items.what: Fixed as a sound demotion, not only documented. Checked against Angular 18.2.14 router.mjs: updateSegmentGroupChildren copies the other root outlets (:1121-1125), matchWithChecks runs canMatch with no reuse check (:3641-3649), and shouldRunGuardsAndResolvers decides re-entry (:3272). For every aux level the source could have open, runningGuards now counts canMatch alongside canDeactivate. A level that re-runs counts its canActivate, the canActivateChild of the open aux levels, and its resolvers (resolves=true). A level re-runs when it is l.always (any runGuardsAndResolvers other than paramsChange or pathParamsChange) or when it is mounted below the root (l.aux !== '/'), where a parent's parameters can change. An aux route mounted at the root under the default mode has nothing that can change, so it is not re-run. The runningGuards doc comment is updated.
items.test: guards-run.test.ts 'a named-outlet route the source has open': /a -> /b is may, and its guard holds both cm (canMatch on popup) and ca (canActivate with runGuardsAndResolvers 'always' on side). It failed on bc40f3c's sources. Mutants that drop the canMatch or the re-run set are both killed.

items.problem: router (b): hidden() let a literal redirect that covers one instance of a parameterised screen hide the whole screen, so /items/:id -> /a fell from must to may.
items.what: overlaps() in matcher.ts takes an optional every flag. With it, a parameter on the address side is matched only by a parameter in the pattern. hidden() now asks redirectsAt and catchAllsAt with every=true. A screen is hidden only when a redirect or catch-all that the router may meet first answers every address the screen stands for. A redirect at /q/:id declared before /q/new still hides it.
items.test: guards-run.test.ts 'a screen a redirect hides': /items/:id -> /a is must and /q/new -> /a is may. It failed on bc40f3c, and the mutant that removes `!every &&` is killed.

items.problem: router (a): four demotion sub-rules had no test that fails when the rule is removed: cumulative consumed segments, preserved forced to 0 after a redirect, tried levels collected at later hops, and a later prefix redirect upgrading an earlier full one.
items.what: Added four tests, one per sub-rule, with fixtures checked against the Angular source (equalParamsAndUrlSegments recurses to parents; an absolute redirect builds a fresh tree, :3578; canMatch runs on routes that are tried and then abandoned). These tests pass on main because the rules already exist. I proved each one by applying its mutant in a scratch run: consumed = l.consumes; dropping && !landed.redirected; if (hop === 0) tried.push; deleting routes.ts `else if (prefix && !first.prefix) Object.assign(...)`. Each mutant made exactly its test fail.
items.test: guards-run.test.ts 'the sub-rules of a shared route being kept' (4 its). The mutation script is /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kanetran29-personal-uigraph/d25f151e-9d40-4c0d-b297-fe3be149d56e/scratchpad/rt/mutants.mjs (M1-M4, all KILLED).

items.problem: router (c): redirectsAt excluded every '**' because a catch-all is supposedly 'matched last'. That is false: Angular matches '**' in declaration order. Component catch-alls were never considered at all.
items.what: Catch-alls are now ordinary rivals in declaration order, both '**' redirects and '**' component screens (the new catchAllsAt). The rivals feed both the landing's ambiguity and hidden(). A catch-all stops being a rival in two cases. (1) It is declared after the answering route in the same table, decided by the generalised before(a, b), which compares two level chains; this makes a '**' declared earlier in the same array sound. (2) It sits in a different table that the root scan walked apart (the new apart(), using a `roots` set collectRoutes now fills). For case (2), the doc comment on apart() states an ASSUMPTION: the router joins separately registered tables in ROUTES-provider order, which the walk does not read, and a catch-all in one is assumed to come after every route of the others. A table spread into another counts as neither, so its catch-all is a rival, which is sound and costs precision. With no screen at the address, the answering redirect's own levels now play the screen's part, so a '**' declared before the redirect makes the landing ambiguous. Measured: with apart() disabled, must edges go k8sdash 125->0 and bitwarden 1->0, so 126 of 150 rest on the assumption. Both apps keep it. bitwarden's app.module.ts imports WildcardRoutingModule last ('Needs to be last'). k8sdash's index.module.ts imports ChromeModule before RouterModule.forRoot(routes).
items.test: guards-run.test.ts 'a catch-all in declaration order'. A '**' redirect or '**' screen before x in the same array gives may. One after x gives must. A root '**' declared before 'old' keeps /old -> /b from being must. This test failed on bc40f3c, and the Fc1/Fc2 mutants are killed. A second test pins the separate-table assumption (must), and the mutant that makes apart() return false is killed.

items.problem: router (d): probe walks now register redirects with a null target. A claimed, unwalked file whose only route is a function-valued redirectTo becomes unplaced and adds an incomplete-route-set note that voids dead-link claims. This was undisclosed and untested.
items.what: I kept the new accounting rather than restoring the old, because the old one was wrong. The old rule already counted a string-valued redirect in such a file as unplaced. A function-valued redirect declares its address just as surely, and leaving it out lets a link to that address be reported as 'matches no declared route', a false dead link. The mintsFromRoot doc comment now says so. Soundiness-note counts per app, before (bc40f3c) and after: realworld {over-approximation 9, async-guard 5} unchanged. alfresco {incomplete-route-set 1, unresolved-component 1, dynamic-target 39, unattributed 3, wildcard-redirect 1} unchanged. ghostfolio {irs 1, dynamic-target 97, wildcard 16, over-approx 1, unattributed 1} unchanged. k8sdash {dynamic-target 15, ambiguous-selector 1, unattributed 1, wildcard 1} unchanged. bitwarden {irs 1, dynamic-target 45, wildcard 84, unresolved-component 1, ambiguous-selector 8, indirect-shell 1, unattributed 11} unchanged. mifos {irs 1, dynamic-target 146, wildcard 81->80, over-approx 144, indirect-shell 1, unattributed 2}. The four incomplete-route-set notes say: alfresco 1 outlet, ghostfolio 1 path + 1 call, bitwarden 1 call, mifos 1 lazy subtree. None of them comes from an unplaced file, before or after, so this accounting voids no app's dead-link census. The old rule is a subset of the new one, so it gives the same counts.
items.test: regressions.test.ts "declares the table unplaced when its only route is a redirect to %s" (string and function). The function case fails under the mutant that makes the probe ignore null-target redirects (Fd, KILLED); the string case is the control.

items.problem: router (e): land() returned target null when an address with no screen is answered by a redirect whose target is not read. The link then went down the catch-all branch, got a may edge to the catch-all, and a wrong 'matches no declared route' note. A link answered only by a parameter or prefix redirect was also reported as reaching no declared route.
items.what: land() now handles an address with no screen and no exact redirect. If exactly one non-catch-all redirect at a pattern or shorter prefix answers it, it is followed through the new matcher.ts redirectAddress(), which fills :params the way applyRedirectCommands/findPosParam do, but only when the pattern consumes the whole address. land() returns unread=true and stops in three cases: the redirect's target is not read; segments are left over (whether they survive depends on whether redirectTo was relative, which the full path does not keep); or several redirects answer. emitTargets then records a dynamic-target note ('literal target "X" is answered by a redirect the reader does not follow, so where it lands is not read') and draws no edge, instead of taking the catch-all branch. The controls-mode caller of land() (wireControlNav) had the same wrong note and got the same fix in the second commit. Skipped: following prefix redirects with leftover segments needs a relative/absolute flag on Redirect, and picking among several pattern redirects by declaration order.
items.test: guards-run.test.ts 'an address only a redirect answers'. With fixture H plus param, prefix-leftover and two-rival cases: no edge to *, no wildcard or unresolved note, three dynamic-target notes, and /a -> /items/:id must. A second it covers controls mode. Both failed on bc40f3c, and the Fe1-Fe4 mutants are killed.

problems.where: packages/adapter-angular/src/matcher.ts redirectAddress(), used by land() in extract.ts (problem e)
problems.what: This change adds a new way to produce a false must edge. redirectAddress fills `:name` from every parameter in the redirect's full path, parent routes included. Angular fills it only from the redirect route's own match (positionalParamSegments). When an absolute redirectTo names a parent's parameter, Angular throws RuntimeError 4001 and the navigation never happens, but the extractor follows the redirect and draws a must edge. The doc comment says a parameter 'the pattern does not bind' is rejected, but the pattern it checks is the full path, not the route's own path. Fix: bind only the redirect route's own consumed segments. This needs a relative/absolute flag, or the raw redirectTo, on Redirect, because a relative target's joined parent prefix is a legitimate copy of the address.
problems.evidence: Probe in a scratch copy, scratchpad/rv/.../zz-probe.test.ts P1. Routes: { path: 'p/:pid', children: [{ path: 'x', redirectTo: '/q/:pid', pathMatch: 'full' }] }, { path: 'q/:id', component: P }, plus a link to '/p/7/x'. HEAD gives `n_a -> n_q_id must`. main (bc40f3c) draws no edge and records `unresolved-target`. In Angular 21 _router-chunk.mjs:3042, the posParams passed to applyRedirectCommands are `positionalParamSegments` from match(segmentGroup, route, segments) for the redirect route alone. findPosParam (:2625-2627) throws 4001 when the name is missing. Angular 18.2.14 router.mjs:3901-3922 is the same.

problems.where: extract.ts land(): the multi-hop loop (pre-existing; extended by this change to pattern redirects)
problems.what: land() follows every redirect on the way. Angular does not apply a second redirect after a relative one: expandSegmentAgainstRouteUsingRedirect re-enters processSegment with allowRedirects=false, and a redirect route then throws NoMatch, so the router backtracks or fails. A relative redirect whose target is another redirect therefore produces a false must. main already had this for exact redirects. The new `patterned` branch extends it to parameter-pattern redirects. Redirect has no relative/absolute flag, so this cannot be fixed without one; the commit notes the missing flag only for the leftover-segments case. k8sdash runs Angular 16.2.1, where chaining after an absolute redirect also differs.
problems.evidence: Probe P2: { path: 'item/:id', redirectTo: 'items/:id' } (relative) -> { path: 'items/:id', redirectTo: '/products/:id' } -> { path: 'products/:id', component: P }, with a link to '/item/5'. HEAD gives must `/a -> /products/:id`. main gives an unresolved note for /item/5 but the same must for the exact chain '/old' -> 'mid' -> '/products/1'. Angular 21 :3008-3017 (`if (this.allowRedirects && allowRedirects) ... throw new NoMatch`) and :3043 (processSegment(..., false, ...)); Angular 18.2.14 router.mjs:3922. Corpus must sets are unchanged before/after (rt/before vs rt/after: 9/0/0/125/1/15), so no measured edge depends on it today.

problems.what: Several sub-rules that this change adds or claims have no test that fails when they are removed. The (f) claim says the mutants dropping 'the re-run set' are killed. That holds only for the whole set: its nested-mount condition, its canActivateChild term and its resolver term each survive on their own. In (c), the catch-all half of hidden(), and the `at.endsWith('*') &&` guard that keeps apart() from dismissing ordinary redirects in another table (a guard that matters for soundness), are also untested.
problems.evidence: Mutation run on a scratch copy (scratchpad/rvtools/mut.mjs + m1.json; baseline 392/392 pass). These mutants SURVIVED with the full suite green: `rerun = closing.filter((l) => l.always)` (drops `|| l.aux !== '/'`), removing `...(rerun.length > 0 ? closing.flatMap((l) => l.canActivateChild) : [])`, removing `|| rerun.some((l) => l.resolve)`, `metFirst` using `apart(...)` without `at.endsWith('*') &&`, hidden() without `+ catchAllsAt(path, first, true).length`, and hidden() with catchAllsAt not using `every`. The claimed mutants M1-M4, Fb, Fc1-3, Fd, Fe1-4 and Ff1 are all killed, as stated.

problems.what: 126 of the 150 corpus must edges (all 125 in k8sdash and the 1 in bitwarden) now rest on an assumption: a '**' in a separately registered table comes after every route of the other tables. The assumption is stated only in a code comment. The tool emits no soundiness note when apart() is used to dismiss a rival. The thesis Claim 3.1 text (ch3-analysis.tex: 'when the address is one that two declared routes, or a route and a redirect, can answer ... demoted') does not mention it. I checked the assumption against the corpus and it holds. k8sdash imports ChromeModule before RouterModule.forRoot(routes), and forRoot's providers are processed after the imports anyway. bitwarden imports WildcardRoutingModule last. main rested on a wider, unstated version of the same assumption, so this is an improvement that still needs to be stated in the thesis or in the soundiness output.
problems.evidence: rt/noapart vs rt/after: k8sdash must 125 -> 0, bitwarden 1 -> 0, the other apps unchanged. Probe P5 (forRoot listed before a forChild feature module) gives must, which is correct because of how Angular's walkProviderTree defers ModuleWithProviders providers.

problems.what: Precision regression: a screen with a '**' component child is now treated as 'never displayed at its own address', so every edge out of it drops to may. Angular does display the screen there, with the catch-all child rendered in its outlet. A redirect child really does replace the screen, but a catch-all screen descendant does not. The rule is sound, but it demotes edges that main kept as must. hidden() should leave out catch-all screens whose chain extends the screen's own chain.
problems.evidence: Probe P12: { path: 'x', component: X, children: [{ path: 'k', component: NF }, { path: '**', component: NF }] }, with X linking to /a. HEAD gives `n_x -> n_a may`; main gives must. No corpus must edge changed.

problems.where: extract.ts emitTargets wildcard branch / land() `patterned` filter (pre-existing, adjacent to problem e)
problems.what: An address answered only by a nested catch-all redirect ('adm/**') is still sent down the root catch-all branch. The extractor draws a may edge to the root catch-all's target and writes a note naming the wrong destination. The reason is that `patterned` drops every '*' redirect and the wildcard branch reads only redirects.get('*').
problems.evidence: Probe P7: adm children [x, { path: '**', redirectTo: '/adm/x' }] plus a root '**' -> '/a', with a link to '/adm/zzz'. Both HEAD and main give `n_a -> n_a may` and the note 'matches no declared route and the wildcard route redirects it to /a'. Angular lands on /adm/x.

commits: 5350856 fix: keep a dropped layout's children inside it, and narrow the unseen-caller join (on top of main bc40f3c, fast-forwarded first; not pushed)

items.problem: major: routes.ts root cause. When two path:'' routes with components sit at one level (bitwarden oss-routing.module.ts:122 Frontend, :158 AnonLayoutWrapper, :682 UserLayout), the walk kept the first route and hung the later routes' children under it. The kept layout was then treated as rendered on screens that Angular only reaches by backtracking into the later route. Probe C gave n_vault>n_login:must.
items.what: Checked against @angular/router 18.2.14 fesm2022/router.mjs:3859-3876. processSegment tries sibling routes in order, turns a NoMatch from a route's children into null, and takes the first route that matches, so it backtracks. The fix is in walkElements (routes.ts). When a route with a component finds its address already taken, it no longer mints a screen. Instead its RouteLevel gets `layout = componentFile`, and its children hang under the screen above it (`childParent = minted ? nodeId : parentNodeId`) rather than under the route holding the address. Each RouteInfo that is minted gets `layouts`, the dropped-layout components on its own level chain, recorded at the moment it is minted. Levels added to a host later are not counted. The address itself ('/') still belongs to the first route. Level chains were already built per actual route object. attribute.ts adds each layout to routeComponentScreens for the screens that list it, so outlet descent, firm nesting and call-graph seeds all follow. extract.ts behindHiddenOutlet now also checks each layout's outlet, and the unplaced-origin set counts layouts as placed.
items.test: callgraph.test.ts 'a layout whose address an earlier route holds': 'keeps the first route's layout off the screens the second one wraps' (probe C: Frontend's /login link sits only on n_root and n_login), 'renders its own links on the screens it wraps, at must, and says no shell is indirect', 'demotes a page it wraps when its outlet is under a condition'. Reverting the walk change makes 5 tests fail. Reverting only the hidden-outlet change makes 1 fail, and reverting only the placed-set change makes 1 fail.

items.problem: major: the #16 lostShell fix went too far. A lost outlet holder, and everything it nests, was never seeded, so navigations reached only through it were lost on the screens it really renders. Probe B gave no edge, and bitwarden lost web-premium-upgrade-prompt.service.ts:85/:99 on 33+ UserLayout screens.
items.what: Once the walk is fixed, bitwarden's AnonLayoutWrapper and UserLayout are route layouts and are seeded with the screens they wrap. Its indirect-shell note goes from 1 to 0. lostShell is still needed, though: mifos's ShellComponent comes in through a wrapper route (Route.withShell returns {path:'', component: ShellComponent, children}), and so would a childless dropped route or a route the walk cannot read. Removing lostShell would make such a holder a firm shell and could produce must edges on screens it never renders, such as /login. So the rule is narrowed instead: the `if (lostShell.has(c.file)) continue` in the seeds is removed, and a remaining lost holder is seeded at top like every other indirect shell. Top over-approximates its unknown screens, and every call-graph emission is capped at may.
items.test: 'seeds what it nests with the screens it wraps, though no routed page calls it' (probe B, with Vault as a leaf). 'is an indirect shell: its links are held at may, and what it nests still reaches the call graph from top' (a withShell-shaped wrapper whose nav calls a bound Prompt, giving n_scope_shell>n_login). Both fail on the pre-fix sources, and the second also fails when only the seeds `continue` is restored.

items.problem: minor: routeNamedComponents matched every `component:` property in any file, so a real root shell named in a widget registry or dialog config was demoted to an indirect shell (probe A).
items.what: Only a `component` property of an object that declares an address (`path` or `matcher`) now counts. The doc comment is updated to match.
items.test: 'is not taken from an object that names the component but declares no address'. The bootstrapped Shell, named in widgets.ts `{ id: 'root', component: Shell }`, keeps n_login>n_x must. This fails on the pre-fix code and when only the route-shape check is reverted.

items.problem: minor: in the call graph, `loaded` filtered bindings and subclasses but not callers. Classes and module-level code in files the application never loads still created call edges and unseen roots (probe SIBLING), and so did a dead member in the service itself (probe DEAD).
items.what: The unloaded-file half is fixed. memberScopes follows calls only from classes and `<module>` code in files that run, meaning the application loads them or they are a seed (`runs`). The dead-member half is left as it was, on purpose. A member with no visible caller cannot be told apart from one that is called where the graph cannot look: a template call through a receiver that is not a field, a method passed as a callback (`subscribe(this.helper)`), or a framework hook. Treating it as an unseen caller is the safe side. It now adds only the join of its own class, every such edge is capped at may, and the cost is precision only. Side effect: the resolution counts no longer include calls in unloaded files (ghostfolio's apps/api, bitwarden's apps/browser and apps/cli). CGDirect/CGBound/CGSubclass/CGUnresolved go from 7023/5904/23/1807 to 5574/4937/18/1111. Per app: ghostfolio direct 1206->365; bitwarden 3030/5902/22/1806 -> 2426/4935/17/1110; alfresco direct 219->215.
items.test: 'reads no caller in a file the application does not load' (memberScopes with a /sibling class and module function: Nav.goA is not unseen and resolved.direct is 1). It fails on the pre-fix code and when only `runs` is reverted.

items.problem: minor: the union of an unseen member with the class join added pairs that cannot occur (bitwarden organization-warnings.service.ts:227, +22). The it.each tests expected n_y>n_a from a guard that no route uses. The class join was keyed by simple class name, so the #15 collision came back.
items.what: The union is narrowed. memberScopes.unseen is now a Map from each member to the files of the unseen roots that reach it (fileOfKey is recorded in keyOf). In extract.ts a placed member adds `joinOf(rootFile)`, which is the components that inject the caller's own classes plus the routes that name it as a guard. That is the same fallback an unreached member gets. A member goes to top when a root file is injected in the shell. The service's own join is no longer used. A caller that nothing injects and no route names (a guard on no route, an unseeded component) therefore adds nothing. In bitwarden that removes the 22 pairs; the 2 pairs from real callers stay. The class join itself (attribute.ts) now resolves injected types through their declarations (injectedClassFiles), replacing fileOfClass by simple name. The old it.each tests are replaced by tests that expect only pairs that can occur: Boot's constructor, a field initialiser, a local, or a helper it hands Nav to, all running when Y is created, give y>a. A guard on y/:id, which runs again when the parameter changes, gives y_id>a.
items.test: 'adds no screen for a guard class / functional guard no route names' (fails on the old union). 'puts it at top when the class of that caller is injected in the shell' (fails on the old top clause and with the top branch deleted). 'joins a class no caller reaches over the components that inject it, not over those that inject a namesake' (fails on the pre-fix name-keyed join). The positive tests are 'adds the screens of the components that inject the class whose %s calls it' x4 and 'adds the screens of the routes that name a guard that calls it...'.

items.problem: minor: parts of the earlier fixes had no test: (a) isLoaded in the subclass fallback, (b) unwrapping array types, (c) the branch that sends unseen plus serviceShell to top, (d) the dead `|| bindings.has(t)` in the unresolved counter.
items.what: (a), (b) and (c) are now covered. (d) is deleted: candidates() never returns null for a bound token, so the clause could not change anything.
items.test: (a) 'resolves an abstract class to no subclass declared in a file the application does not load' kills the subclass-loaded mutant. (b) 'reads no class from an array type...' kills the mutant that unwraps array types. (c) 'puts it at top when the class of that caller is injected in the shell' kills both top-branch mutants. All 12 mutants in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kanetran29-personal-uigraph/d25f151e-9d40-4c0d-b297-fe3be149d56e/scratchpad/cg/mutate.py are killed, and 10 of the new tests fail on the bc40f3c sources.

Fail-before evidence:

- **ch3-analysis.tex:484-494 (shell rule).**
  - Add that a route whose address an earlier route holds (a second or third `{path:'', component}` at one level) renders its component on the screens it declares. Angular backtracks into it (router.mjs:3859-3876). It is a layout and not a shell, and the earlier route's layout is not rendered there.
  - An outlet holder now counts as "named by a route" only through an object that declares a `path` or `matcher`. Such a holder (for example a wrapper-returned route) is an indirect shell, capped at may, and is now seeded at top in the call graph. It is no longer left unseeded.

- **ch3-analysis.tex:509-519 (call graph).**
  - Callers are read only from files the application loads, or that are seeds.
  - A member that a caller the graph cannot see also reaches takes the union with the join of that caller's own file: the components that inject its classes, plus the routes that name it as a guard, or top when the shell injects it. It no longer takes the service's own class join. A caller that nothing injects and no route names adds nothing.
  - The class join now resolves injected types through their declarations, not by simple name.

- **ch6-discussion.tex:578-587.**
  - ":580 widens a scope and never narrows it" is false.
  - ":583-584 falls back to the join over every component that injects its class" holds only when no caller resolves. For unseen members it is the unseen caller's class join.
  - The simple-name keying listed as a limitation is gone.
  - ch6:214 (shell rule capped at may where the mounting route is invisible) now refers only to wrapper, unreadable and childless routes. Dropped siblings are layouts.

problems.what: Claim 3.1 regression. A dropped layout's own links now go through the descendants loop, which emits them at must and never checks behindHiddenOutlet for the outlets above the layout. When the layout sits under a host or ancestor whose primary outlet is inside @if, its links come out must on screens where it renders only some of the time. In the same case the page it wraps is correctly demoted to may, and main gave the layout may as an indirect shell. The underlying bug already exists for minted route components on their descendant screens. This diff routes layouts into that path. The new test 'demotes a page it wraps when its outlet is under a condition' covers only the page's links, never the layout's.
problems.evidence: Probe file /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kanetran29-personal-uigraph/d25f151e-9d40-4c0d-b297-fe3be149d56e/scratchpad/k2rv366x2/zprobe.test.ts. problems.what: A layout that is an empty-path child with a component under a screen (the host case) renders on the host's own address. Angular matches it there through NoLeftoversInUrl (router.mjs: `new TreeNode(snapshot, child instanceof TreeNode ? [child] : [])`). The walk adds the layout's guards to host.levels but never adds the component to host.layouts, because layouts are fixed when the host is minted. So the layout's links on the host screen disappear without any note. On main they were may, with an indirect-shell note. This contradicts the new RouteInfo.layouts doc, which lists 'an empty-path child with a component under a screen'.

problems.what: The narrowing treats 'no component injects the root's file and no route names it' as 'the root never runs'. Many such callers do run: functional and class HTTP interceptors (thesis Table: interceptor scope = top), provideAppInitializer/APP_INITIALIZER code, a useClass-bound implementation whose constructor calls the service (components inject the abstract token's file, never the impl's), and services injected only by other services. Their contribution is now empty and no soundiness note is emitted. Main still covered them through the service's own join. The edited comment itself names 'an interceptor' as an unseen caller, and the new rule gives it nothing. Every edge involved is may, so Claim 3.1 is unaffected, but this is an unannounced loss of real edges.
problems.evidence: Probe file zprobe.test.ts in the same scratch folder. X calls nav.goA() in a handler; Y injects Nav but does not call it. INTERCEPT (withInterceptors([fn calling inject(Nav).goA()])), INIT (provideAppInitializer), CLSINT (HTTP_INTERCEPTORS useClass), TRANS (Y->Svc2->Boot whose constructor calls goA) and BOUNDIMPL ({provide: Prompt, useClass: WebPrompt}, WebPrompt's constructor calls goA, Y injects Prompt) all give ['n_x>n_a:may'] on new, against ['n_x>n_a:may','n_y>n_a:may'] on main. problems.what: The check counts a `component:` only when the same literal has a `path`/`matcher` property. A real route that gets its path from a spread (`{ ...BASE, component: Shell, children }`) no longer counts. The walk already drops such routes silently, so Shell is then elected a firm shell, and its links become must on every screen, including screens it never renders. That violates Claim 3.1. On main the broad match kept it a lost shell, held at may.
problems.evidence: Probe file zprobe2.test.ts in the same scratch folder, case SPREAD: routes [{...BASE, component: Shell, children:[x]}, {path:'login'}, {path:'about'}], where Shell has <a routerLink=/login> and an outlet. New gives n_about>n_login:must with no note. Main gave n_about>n_login:may plus an indirect-shell note. Angular never renders Shell on /about. Fix: also accept an object that has a SpreadAssignment.

problems.what: The claim that bitwarden's AnonLayoutWrapper becomes a route layout seeded with the screens it wraps is false. Its componentFile resolves to the barrel libs/components/src/index.ts, because resolveImportedFile returns the module specifier file and does not follow re-exports. The barrel is recorded as the layout, so the real component gets no screens and is neither seeded nor placed. This is not a regression, since its output is identical to main, but the layout mechanism inherits the barrel bug. Using declarationsOf on the component identifier would fix it.
problems.evidence: Corpus scan with the new collectRoutes: bitwarden distinctLayouts = ['../../libs/components/src/index.ts','src/app/layouts/user-layout.component.ts'], and the host-case level at '/2fa' also resolves to index.ts. bitwarden.db on new and on main: 0 edges witnessed in anon-layout files, and an identical unplaced-origin list (o_LoginComponent, o_SsoComponent, ...). Only UserLayout explains the indirect-shell 1->0 change.

problems.what: The new rule (an unseen member runs where its root's file runs, and goes to top when the root is injected in the shell) applies only to members the call graph places. A member reached only from unseen roots falls to `rest` and still uses the service's own join(f) and joinTop(f). So a constructor of a shell-injected Boot that calls a member nothing else calls is not sent to top. The 'same fallback' rationale is applied in only one direction. This behaviour was already on main, but it is now inconsistent with the narrowed rule.
problems.evidence: Reading the code: `rest = ts.filter(t => !atTop.includes(t) && !byMember.includes(t))`, then `joinTop`/`joinScreens` of f. unseenFrom(t) is never consulted for unplaced t.

problems.what: The fix makes an unread target 'neither a pass nor a failure' only for must sites. An unread may site, or one on an unknown-modality edge, still goes to ok++ and counts as clean in both the numerator and the denominator of 'Clean of judged'. So the claim that an unread site is neither a pass nor a failure in either column is false, and judgedSites' doc ('the sites on which the check reached a verdict about the target') does not describe what it counts. The diff's own arrayTarget change makes this worse: sites that were TARGET_MISMATCH become 'clean' although their target is now unread.
problems.evidence: I ran the new witness-check, instrumented, on the six current corpus maps (~/personal/uigraph-corpus, with --routes). 465 sites reach ok++ with agrees===null: alfresco 16, ghostfolio 182, k8sdash 53, bitwarden 62, mifos 152. About 130 of these are may edges into resolved routes and the rest are unknown edges. With them taken out, the corpus clean-of-judged share falls from 1559/1938 (80.4%) to 1094/1473 (74.3%). Old vs new on bitwarden: two may sites go from TARGET_MISMATCH to clean, src/app/billing/services/web-premium-upgrade-prompt.service.ts:99 `navigate([this.subscriptionPageRoute])` and upgrade-flow.service.ts:53 `navigate([SELF_HOST_SUBSCRIPTION_URL])`. Neither target is read.

problems.what: The null rule fires only when the literal parts contain nothing but '/'. A relative array whose only literal is a dot segment, `['./', id]`, `['../', id]` or `['..', id]`, has no literal segment either, but is still read as one `:param` under the source or parent screen. It therefore agrees with any one-segment literal child or sibling route, which is the same 'must witness passes without its target being read' defect the fix claims to close. A dynamic head followed by a literal, `[base, 'edit']`, is also read with the segments reordered ('edit/:param'), although Angular splits the first command on '/' and it may be absolute.
problems.evidence: Fixture with three must router-link edges from /p/a. `['../', id]` against /p/settings: clean (not TARGET_UNREAD). `['./', id]` against /p/a/settings: clean. `[base, 'edit']` against /edit/x: TARGET_MISMATCH 'targets /p/a/edit/:param'. Output: tally {TARGET_MISMATCH:1}, mustUnread 0. None of the current corpus must sites has a :param answering a literal destination segment (91 may sites do), so no published figure moves today.

problems.what: A must-unattributed row is never refused for being stale. Exact mode skips it in the 'listed but earns no must edge' loop, and subset mode allows absence, so such a row can outlive its construct, unlike `must` rows ('so the file cannot go stale'). The sibling deadlock also remains: a construct that is must in both graphs but reaches an extra address without attribution fails exact mode if that address is recorded and subset mode if it is not.
problems.evidence: Code reading: `listed` holds must-unattributed rows only when !exact, and the `if (exact)` stale loop iterates `listed`. The extra-target check is `missing.length || (exact && extra.length)`, so one target set cannot satisfy both graphs. Neither case occurs at this commit: all 25 rows are 'must', and both census modes pass on the current corpus (150 must).

problems.what: A run with no Tests line, from a timeout or a vitest crash, is recorded as survived:false. judge's comment says such a run is not a kill, yet sweep-to-latex counts it as covered. Also, `--only` given as the last argument with no value leaves `only` undefined, so the script runs the full sweep and overwrites results-must/mutation-sweep.json, which the partial-run guard is meant to prevent.
problems.evidence: judge returns { survived: false, killedBy: 'the suite did not run' }, and sweep-to-latex has covered = m.survived === false. flag('--only') returns argv[i+1], which is undefined when the flag is last, so out falls back to DEFAULT_OUT.
